chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from al-Ḥuṣayn ibn Abī al-Ḥuṣayn, who said:

I wrote to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: May I be made your ransom, your followers have differed regarding the salat (prayer) of al-fajr. Some of them pray when the first dawn rises, extending upward in the sky, while some of them pray when it spreads across the lower horizon and becomes clear. I do not know which of the two times is better so that I may pray in it. So if you see fit, O my master—may Allah make me your ransom—to teach me the better of the two times, and to specify for me what I should do when there is moonlight and the dawn does not become clear until it reddens and morning comes, and what I should do with the moon, and what the limit of that is in travel and residence, then do so, if Allah wills.

So he wrote in his own hand: Al-fajr, may Allah have mercy on you, is the white thread, and it is not the whiteness rising upward. Do not pray, whether in travel or residence, until you clearly discern it—may Allah have mercy on you—for Allah has not left His creation in doubt concerning this.
For He said: “Eat and drink until the white thread becomes distinct to you from the black thread at dawn.”
So the white thread is the dawn by which eating and drinking become forbidden in sawm (fasting), and likewise it is that which makes salat (prayer) obligatory.

key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, mentioned to clarify that the same ruling applies while traveling
key_terms.الصِّيَامِ: fasting, for which eating and drinking become forbidden at true dawn
key_terms.الْحَضَرِ: residence, mentioned alongside travel to indicate the ruling is general
key_terms.الْخَيْطُ الْأَبْيَضُ: the true dawn, the visible white line across the horizon that marks the legal beginning of fasting and prayer
key_terms.الْخَيْطِ الْأَسْوَدِ: the darkness of night distinguished from the true dawn
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ الْأَوَّلُ: the first dawn, described here as the upward-extending light that is not the prayer time
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْفَجْرِ: the fajr prayer whose beginning time is being asked about

ai.seo_question: When does the time of Salat al-Fajr begin according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith explains that the valid time of fajr begins with the true dawn, identified as the horizontal white thread spread across the horizon, not the vertical light rising upward. It connects the beginning of fajr prayer with the same sign that marks the start of fasting, grounding the ruling in the Qur'anic expression of the white thread and black thread.
